principles: Fix the guard, not the correct code: the failing assertion reflects a defect in the smoke, not the command catalog.
Single source of truth: the dispatch enum already derives from AGENT_DISPATCH_ACCEPTED_TYPES; the smoke must respect that same source rather than the raw registry.
Guard both directions: coverage must catch a stale non-dispatchable agent leaking into the enum AND a retired lane being wrongly accepted.
No new build cost and no silent regressions: reuse validate's existing build step and wire the smoke so future divergence fails loudly.
drivers: The retirement of lattice-review-channel is deliberate (ACCEPTED_TYPES filter + resolveAgentDispatchType) and must not be undone.
The smoke is currently absent from validate.commands, so this regression class is unguarded.
The smoke spawns real CLI subprocesses, so it belongs on the normal validate tier, not the fast focus set.

options.name: Add lattice-review-channel to the dispatch enum (originally proposed)
pros: One-line change targeting the failing assertion at line 159
cons: Un-retires a deliberately-retired agent, contradicting the ACCEPTED_TYPES filter and resolveAgentDispatchType
Does not even make the smoke pass: line 161 validateAgentDispatchRequest still throws retired for channel
Violates bidirectional consistency: a stale non-dispatchable agent would be silently accepted

options.name: Skip the retired entry in the smoke loop
cons: Adds no reverse guard; a future stale non-dispatchable agent leaking into the enum would pass unnoticed

options.name: Bidirectional-consistency guard
pros: Smoke exits 0 while respecting the retirement
Actively asserts retired entries are rejected by BOTH the dispatch schema and the runtime contract, pinning the retirement
Covers future additions/retirements without editing the smoke (predicate derived from ACCEPTED_TYPES membership)
cons: Slightly more code than a bare skip
Reverse branch currently exercises only lattice-review-channel

rationale: The catalog is already correct and channel's retirement is deliberate, so the fix belongs in the smoke. A bare skip leaves the reverse direction unguarded; the bidirectional guard makes the smoke pass, pins the retirement, and catches future enum/registry divergence, matching the user's stated acceptance criteria. Wiring it into validate.commands (normal tier, timeoutMs 180000 like sibling CLI-subprocess smokes) closes the silent-failure gap without a new build dependency.

preMortem.scenario: The reverse assertion silently stops testing anything
preMortem.trigger: A future refactor makes every registry entry dispatchable, so the retired else-branch becomes dead
preMortem.consequence: The retired-consistency guard no longer exercises any entry
preMortem.mitigation: Derive both branches from ACCEPTED_TYPES membership so a dead else-branch means channel was un-retired, which is itself a reviewable authority change.

preMortem.scenario: Adding the smoke to validate.commands slows or flakes validate
preMortem.trigger: The smoke spawns several CLI subprocesses and compares help output
preMortem.mitigation: Place it on the normal (non-fast) tier with timeoutMs=180000 matching siblings; the smoke uses fixed inputs and self-cleans its tmp dir.

preMortem.scenario: The fix accidentally edits command-catalog.ts or the registry
preMortem.trigger: Temptation to make the enum accept channel to satisfy an assertion
preMortem.consequence: A deliberately-retired agent becomes dispatchable, an authority regression
preMortem.mitigation: Scope boundary excludes those files; the DEV diff must touch only command-catalog-smoke.ts and lattice.config.json.
